Low-level functions in survalis

Source: R/survalis-lowlevel.R
survalis-lowlevel.Rd

survalis 1.3.0 introduced the seven-verb interface – fit(), predict(), evaluate(), tune(), compare(), interpret(), estimate() – plus the resampling constructors (cv(), holdout(), group_cv(), bootstrap()).

Details

The granular functions listed below are the machinery those verbs are built on. They stay exported and supported for direct use, for example in simulation code that calls one learner many times.

Mapping

Low-levelVerb
fit_<learner>()fit(formula, data, model = "<learner>")
predict_<learner>()predict(fit, newdata, times, type)
tune_<learner>()tune(formula, data, model = "<learner>", grid)
cv_survlearner(), cv_summary(), cv_plot()evaluate(...)
score_survmodel()evaluate(fit, resampling = ...)
benchmark(), benchmark_default_survlearners(), benchmark_tuned_survlearners()compare(...)
summarise_benchmark(), summarize_benchmark_results(), best_survlearner()summary() / print() on a survalis_compare
compute_*() / plot_*()interpret(fit, method = ...) then plot()
estimate_rmst()estimate(..., estimand = "RMST_diff")
